message.content:
Below is a quick reference to the **long‑weekend** holidays that Canadians typically enjoy in 2023.  
(These are the federal holidays that fall on a weekday, creating a three‑day weekend. Some provinces observe additional holidays, but the list below covers the nationwide “long‑weekend” events.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | **Yes** – New Year’s Eve (Dec 31) + New Year’s Day (Jan 1) + New Year’s Day (Jan 2) |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, etc.) | Feb 20 | Monday | **Yes** – Family Day (Feb 20) + weekend |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | **Yes** – Good Friday + Easter Saturday + Easter Sunday |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | **Yes** – Victoria Day (May 22) + weekend |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | **Yes** – Canada Day (Jul 1) + weekend |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | **Yes** – Labour Day (Sep 4) + weekend |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | **Yes** – Thanksgiving (Oct 9) + weekend |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Monday | **Yes** – Remembrance Day (Nov 11) + weekend |
| Christmas | Dec 25 | Monday | **Yes** – Christmas (Dec 25) + weekend |

### Quick Tips for Your App
1. **Highlight the weekend days** (Friday–Sunday or Thursday–Saturday) that are adjacent to each holiday.  
2. **Add a note** for holidays that fall on a weekend (e.g., New Year’s Day, Canada Day) – the “long weekend” is the preceding or following weekend.  
3. **Allow users to filter by province** if they want to see provincial holidays (e.g., Family Day in BC, St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, etc.).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the provincial variations or any other details!
